q: EngramBench, the first capability-grounded benchmark governed by the strict axiom of capability overlap without solution overlap.
r: Include: new benchmark with a new evaluation protocol (CCPF, cost and efficiency metrics, repeated trials) for coding agents building multi-layer applications, so a contribution to the evaluation method.

q: we propose RuleEvolve, a self-evolving framework for coding rules.
r: Include: coding rules for AI coding agents are a context mechanism (group b), which EC6 does not narrow.

q: Every setting runs the same 277 SWE-Bench tasks from 6 repositories
r: EC6: a new cost-control technique evaluated on SWE-Bench issue repair, which is always excluded.
Include: controlled comparison of compaction strategies and models on ProgramBench (building a tool from scratch, project level), with repeated runs and a rule-retention analysis.

q: We first ran 30 coding-agent sessions and collected 125 proposals from /retro.
r: Include: empirical study of how coding agents adapt their harness (instructions, skills, executable checks) from experience, a context mechanism with coding agents (group b).

q: This paper presents an empirical study of 42 trajectory-reduction configurations, focusing on their effects on effectiveness, agent behavior, and cost.
r: EC6: evaluation is on SWE-bench style issue repair, which is always excluded.

q: We analyzed the initial instruction stacks of 1,886 releases across five coding agents.
r: Include: longitudinal study of the instructions (system prompts, tool definitions, instruction files) that coding agents send their models, a context mechanism with coding agents (group b).

q: we constructed CASE-Bench, an executable and annotated benchmark for studying how repository context affects the security of LLM-generated code.
r: EC6: the evaluated task is security of generated code (CVE-based), which is always excluded; the context is retrieved repository code, not instruction files.

q: We expose AST, call graph, dependency, documentation, and hybrid repository views as MCP tools
r: EC6: tasks are fault localization, issue repair, test generation and security patching, none of which is feature or project-level development.

q: We train CAMP-II-4B and CAMP-II-9B from Qwen3.5 models of matching size.
r: IC1: on-policy distillation of file-based memory for general long-horizon agents (shop, research, visual), with coding only one environment among five; not SDD, context files or coding-agent evaluation.
